text:
alyssa: Heads up — I spotted a reproducible double-charge where a provisional credit from the sentinel heartbeat gets confirmed again after a route failover + client resume. Repro steps below, short thread to decide mitigation + console/telemetry changes.

sam: Can you drop the logs you saw?

alyssa: sure — clipped logs: 
```
[1728754310] sentinel INFO heartbeat session=abc123 route=router-42 prefetched_tokens=15 trace=tx786
[1728754320] router WARN fallback route -> router-99 session=abc123 reason=instance_unhealthy
[1728754330] ledger INFO provisional_credit session=abc123 tokens=15 trace=tx789 owner=router-42
[1728754360] client INFO reconnect session=abc123 resume=true resume_id=rsm-55
[1728754370] ledger INFO confirmed_charge session=abc123 tokens=15 trace=tx790 owner=router-99
```

alyssa: So provisional credited under owner router-42, then after failover router-99 confirmed the same content and both show in the ledger.

ben: Is this happening during model-swap canaries or just routing flaps?

miko: Looks like sentinel prefetch (heartbeat-triggered) marks provisional on the route it touched. If router flips, the new router doesn't know about the provisional owner and just confirms. Two ideas: require ownership match for confirm OR dedupe confirms using a resume token.

sam: We already attach `resume_id` in the client reconnect handshake (eg `rsm-55` above) but I don't think ledger confirm currently consumes it. Ledger keys today are `session_id + prefix` only.

alyssa: Proposed quick fixes: 
- Option A: add `provisional_owner` metadata to provisional rows and make confirm require owner match (or transfer).
- Option B: require `resume_id` on confirm and dedupe by `session_id+resume_id`.

miko: Option B seems safer for cross-router confirms — resume_id is globally unique per resume attempt. But we'd need to populate it everywhere (stream resume, toolcall resume, etc.).

ben: Concern: schema change to ledger (new index on resume_id) — needs migration/backfill strategy. Maybe implement confirm-time lookup: if `resume_id` present, check dedupe index; if not present, fallback to existing behavior. That keeps backward compatibility.

ops-bot: PROD incident RL-3421 created for duplicate-charge spikes. Assigned @sam, priority P2.

jessica: Console UX: right now provisional vs confirmed show as separate rows — that confuses customers. We should add a "linked view" that groups provisional->confirmed transitions and shows `resume_id`, `owner_history` and a trace link to the request. Quick mock would help support debug.

sam: Telemetry ask: emit a sampled event when confirmed_charge occurs but no matching provisional record exists, e.g. metric `ledger.confirm_mismatch` with `trace_id`, `session_id`, `resume_id` (if present). That will help us triage.

alyssa: Quick mitigation options: 
- make sentinel prefetch conservative (only prefetch after 2 stable heartbeats) — reduces false provisional but increases latency; or
- router on takeover could query previous owner for outstanding provisonals during a short handoff window (complicated).

miko: We can try sentinel cooldown first as an interim. Long-term: resume_id dedupe + owner metadata is better.

ben: Also flag: toolcall confirm path uses a different ledger API. Audit that path — toolcalls might be confirming without resume semantics, so they could be another source of double-charge.

amy: noted — I'll add a bullet for toolcall ledger audit.

sam: Action items (rough):
- sam: implement confirm-time dedupe using `resume_id` (canary, router + ledger checks). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 (WIP)
- miko: add `ledger.confirm_mismatch` metric + 1% sampled event with traces. (2w)
- jessica: mock console "linked view" and add resume_id/owner_history display (EOD draft)
- alyssa: run failure-injection load test with route flaps + resume to confirm repro and verify canary fix
- amy: audit toolcall confirm path for resume semantics

sam: I'll try to get the canary in the next 48 hours, low-risk toggle.

miko: Also putting a quick dashboard alert: fire if `confirm_mismatch` > 0 for 5m -> page on escalation.

ben: TL;DR: root cause = sentinel prefetch provisional + route failover + client resume causing two different routers to claim credit. Fix via resume_id idempotency + owner metadata; short-term reduce sentinel eagerness.

alyssa: Thanks everyone. I'll attach test traces when I run the load job. Tagging @miko @sam @ben for follow-ups. :raised_hands:

sam: ack. will update thread with PR and canary results.

miko: ack, started a tracking ticket RL-3421-1 for metrics + dashboard work.

(around 1728754987) jessica: mock uploaded: https://figma.redwood.ai/file/console/linked-ledger-view — comments welcome.
